subject: ACME on-prem audit: request for IaC proofpack and runbook
messages:
From: Alice Barnes <alice.barnes@acme-corp.com>
To: neha_kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>, jordan_blake <jordan_blake@redwood.com>
Cc: ACME Security <security@acme-corp.com>
Date: 2026-06-15T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: ACME on-prem audit: request for IaC proofpack and runbook

Hi Neha / Jordan,

We're preparing for an internal compliance run in two weeks and ACME Security has asked us to surface an "IaC proofpack" for the private (on-prem/VPC) deployment we scoped with Redwood. Specifically we need evidence and runnable artifacts that show: 
- Terraform modules for networking (VPC/subnets, IPAM/bgp/routing, bastion access) and their current committed versions; state storage/encryption config and drift history.
- Helm charts used for the API/ingress/internal proxies (values files for production, chart provenance/SBOM).
- Ansible playbooks for host prep and package pinning (with vault usage pattern).
- CI evidence: pipeline IDs, successful gate runs, unit/integration test artifacts, and links to the artifacts stored (build IDs).
- Artifact signing / provenance (cosign or similar), and any attestations (SLSA/Provenance) we can provide.
- A concise runbook for emergency rollback, plus the expected RTO/RPO and escalation contacts.

Can your team produce a bundle with a simple spreadsheet mapping module -> owner -> commit id -> last-tested-pipeline, plus the runbook and any signature bundles? ACME would like the bundle delivered by end of day 2026-06-17.

Also, please call out any gaps we should prioritize for the compliance review (e.g., unsigned modules, missing pipeline logs, incomplete SBOM). If useful, we can do a 30-minute workshop to walk through the artifacts.

Thanks,
Alice Barnes
Senior Cloud Security Engineer
Acme Corporation
From: neha_kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>
To: Alice Barnes <alice.barnes@acme-corp.com>, jordan_blake <jordan_blake@redwood.com>
Cc: ACME Security <security@acme-corp.com>, marissa_cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, irene_choi <irene_choi@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-06-15T11:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: ACME on-prem audit: request for IaC proofpack and runbook

Hi Alice — thanks for the clear ask. We're on it. Quick plan:
1) I'll own the deliverable bundling (proofpack spreadsheet + manifest + runbook).
2) Jordan will collect the Terraform/Helm/Ansible references and pipeline links.
3) Marissa will run the artifact-signing export and package the cosign signatures.
4) Irene will validate the runbook rollback steps against our production playbook and surface any gaps.

A couple of clarifying questions:
- Do you need full pipeline logs or are links + pipeline artifacts (tarred test outputs) sufficient?
- For runbook format, do you prefer a single markdown document or a set of short runbook fragments per subsystem?

We aim to deliver the first-cut bundle by EOD 2026-06-17. If ACME wants the 30-minute workshop, we can schedule on 2026-06-18 morning PST.

Best,
Neha Kapoor
Manager, Private Deployment Security
Redwood Inference
From: jordan_blake <jordan_blake@redwood.com>
To: neha_kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>, Alice Barnes <alice.barnes@acme-corp.com>
Cc: marissa_cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, irene_choi <irene_choi@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-06-16T08:27:00-07:00
Subject: Re: ACME on-prem audit: request for IaC proofpack and runbook

On Tue, Jun 15, 2026 at 11:03 AM neha_kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com> wrote:
> Hi Alice — thanks for the clear ask. We're on it. Quick plan:

Hi all — adding the technical checklist we will attach to the proofpack and notes on known gaps:
- Terraform: export of module commits (modules/networking/*, modules/bastion/*, modules/ipam/*). We'll include state backend metadata (S3/GCS path or on-prem backend), KMS key ID, and last-apply timestamp.
- Helm: chart tarballs + values-production.yaml and a generated SBOM (we use syft for chart images). We'll include Chart provenance and chart-repo commit.
- Ansible: playbook tarball (host-prep, sysctl, package pinning) and vault key handling summary (we don't share secrets).
- CI: GitLab pipeline IDs and a tar of job artifacts (unit/integration test results). We will not include raw secrets; artifacts will be scrubbed.
- Signing/provenance: cosign signatures for container images and a tar of cosign signatures for charts. For Terraform module signatures we will include GPG/cosign attestations where present; we'll also list unsigned modules.
- Runbook: a single markdown runbook with linkable sections (network rollback, helm rollback, host reprovision). We'll include an abbreviated on-call escalation table.

Known gaps to call out to ACME:
- One networking module (modules/ipam/static-assignment) is missing a recorded cosign signature.
- SR-IOV config snippets used in edge racks are in an experimental branch and not yet part of the tagged release; we'll flag it.
- A couple of pipeline artifacts exceed retention and need to be re-created (we'll re-run the test job to capture artifacts if ACME prefers).

Attachments we'll include: "iac-evidence-checklist.xlsx" (spreadsheet mapping), "terraform-module-signatures.tar.gz" (signatures where available).

We can provide the initial bundle to the Drive link Neha will create; happy to run the workshop on 6/18.

—Jordan
Principal SRE, Redwood Inference
From: Alice Barnes <alice.barnes@acme-corp.com>
To: neha_kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>, jordan_blake <jordan_blake@redwood.com>
Cc: ACME Security <security@acme-corp.com>
Date: 2026-06-17T14:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: ACME on-prem audit: request for IaC proofpack and runbook

Thanks — this looks good and exactly the level of detail we need. A couple of small asks before you finalize: 
- Please include the runbook diff (what changed in the last 90 days) as a patch; a short patch file is easiest for our auditors.
- In the spreadsheet, add a column for "last-verified-by" (who ran the test) and a link to the ticket or pipeline that verified it.

If you can drop the bundle into the Drive folder and ping this thread when done, we'll review and then schedule the 30-minute workshop (6/18 morning PT works). Also include a preferred on-call contact (phone + slack handle) for the escalation table.

Appreciate the quick turnaround — ACME Security

--
Alice Barnes
Senior Cloud Security Engineer, Acme Corporation
security@acme-corp.com
